core.about.intro.0: E & I: Expat, Relocation and Immigration Services The Netherlands began with a simple observation from inside the embassy world: the people who move countries best are the ones who are personally accompanied. Not case-managed. Accompanied.
core.about.intro.1: Today Johanna and her network guide professionals, couples, families and founders into the Netherlands, with a specialism no one else claims: Rotterdam, Europoort and the industrial region around Europe’s largest port.

When a landlord calls, we answer in Dutch. When something happens at eleven at night in your first week, the WhatsApp line is the same person who collected you from the airport.

core.about.history.heading: Operating since 2016
core.about.history.text.0: E & I was founded in 2016 and has been guiding arrivals into the Netherlands ever since. A decade in one region is why we know which municipality asks for which document, which landlords will consider an applicant whose contract starts next month, and how long the IND is really taking in the month you apply.

immigration.services.0.title: Highly Skilled Migrant Visa Netherlands
immigration.services.0.metaTitle: Highly Skilled Migrant Visa Netherlands | Personal Guidance
immigration.services.0.metaDescription: Moving to the Netherlands as a highly skilled migrant? We coordinate with your employer, prepare your IND application and guide your family through every step.
immigration.services.0.intro.0: The highly skilled migrant route is the fastest, cleanest way for international professionals to work in the Netherlands. Your employer must be an IND recognized sponsor, your salary must meet the current IND threshold for your age group, and the paperwork must be right the first time.
immigration.services.0.intro.1: That is where we come in. We coordinate directly with your employer’s HR team, prepare you and your family for every appointment, and stay reachable on our 24/7 personal WhatsApp line whenever a question comes up, whatever the time zone.
immigration.services.0.cardText: The fastest work route to the Netherlands, coordinated between you, your employer and the IND.
immigration.services.0.explainer.title: What is the highly skilled migrant permit?
immigration.services.0.explainer.text.0: The highly skilled migrant permit, kennismigrant in Dutch, is the route the Netherlands uses to bring in experienced professionals quickly. It is not judged on your job title or your diploma. It is judged on one thing: whether a Dutch employer that the IND has recognised as a sponsor is paying you above a set salary threshold.
immigration.services.0.explainer.text.1: Because the employer carries the recognition, the procedure is fast and there is no labour market test. The permit is tied to that employer, so it is the contract, not the person, that anchors your residence in the Netherlands.

immigration.services.0.included.title: What we take care of
immigration.services.0.included.blocks.0: Before anything is filed we verify that your employer is a recognized sponsor and that your offer meets the current IND salary threshold, which is indexed every year.
immigration.services.0.included.blocks.1: The sponsor formally submits the application. We prepare the file with HR, chase what is missing and keep both sides on one timeline.
immigration.services.0.included.blocks.2: Your partner and children apply alongside you. We bundle the applications so the whole family lands with the right permits at the same time.
immigration.services.0.included.blocks.3: Birth and marriage certificates often need legalization or an apostille from your home country. We tell you exactly which stamp, from which authority, before you fly.
immigration.services.0.included.blocks.4: Biometrics, permit collection, municipality registration and BSN. We schedule them in the right order and go with you.
immigration.services.0.process.title: How it works
immigration.services.0.process.steps.0.t: We review your offer, your nationality and your family situation, then map the exact route and timeline.
immigration.services.0.process.steps.1.t: We assemble the documents with you and your employer and submit through the sponsor.
immigration.services.0.process.steps.2.t: Depending on your nationality you collect an entry visa at the Dutch embassy before travelling. We prepare you for that appointment.
immigration.services.0.process.steps.3.t: Within your first days we complete registration, permit pickup and the practical essentials.
immigration.services.0.fees.title: Professional fees for a highly skilled migrant application
immigration.services.0.fees.includes.0: Assessment of the salary criterion that applies to your age and situation
immigration.services.0.fees.includes.1: The full application file prepared and filed through your recognised sponsor
immigration.services.0.fees.includes.2: Coordination with your employer’s HR so the contract and start date line up
immigration.services.0.fees.includes.3: Follow-up on every IND request until the decision is issued
immigration.services.0.note: Many highly skilled migrants qualify for the 30% facility, a Dutch tax advantage for incoming employees. Conditions change regularly, so we flag it during intake and connect you with a tax advisor rather than promising numbers.
immigration.services.0.conditions.title: What the IND requires
immigration.services.0.conditions.intro: This route runs through your employer rather than through you. These conditions decide the file before it is ever opened.
Your employer must be an IND recognised sponsor. Without that recognition the route is closed, whatever your salary.
Gross monthly salary from 5,942 euro if you are 30 or older, and from 4,357 euro if you are under 30 (2026, excluding the 8 percent holiday allowance).
A reduced criterion of 3,122 euro applies in the year after a Dutch orientation year or a Dutch degree.
Salary must be paid monthly into a Dutch bank account. Bonuses, allowances and expense budgets do not count towards the threshold.
The 30 percent ruling is calculated on top of the criterion and can never be used to reach it.
Thresholds are indexed every 1 January and judged on the figures in force when the application is filed.
immigration.services.0.details.title: Details worth knowing
immigration.services.0.details.items.0.q: What if my employer is not a recognised sponsor?
immigration.services.0.details.items.0.a: Recognition takes weeks that a start date rarely has. When an employer is not recognised we look at the EU Blue Card, which carries no sponsorship requirement, or we run the recognition application alongside your file if the company intends to hire internationally again.
immigration.services.0.details.items.1.q: How fast is the decision in practice?
immigration.services.0.details.items.1.a: Recognised sponsors have a legal decision term of ninety days, and complete files are frequently decided in two to four weeks. The delay in this route is almost always a missing legalised document, not the IND.
immigration.services.0.details.items.2.q: What happens when I change jobs?
immigration.services.0.details.items.2.a: Your permit is tied to your employer. A new employer must also be a recognised sponsor and must file a new application, and you may not start before it is approved. We manage the switch so there is no gap in your residence.
immigration.services.0.details.items.3.q: Do I need an MVV as well as the permit?
immigration.services.0.details.items.3.a: Most non-EU nationals do, and we apply for both in a single combined procedure. Nationals of the United States, Canada, Japan, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea and the United Kingdom are exempt and travel on the permit alone.
immigration.services.0.faq.title: Questions we hear often
immigration.services.0.faq.items.0.q: Can my partner work in the Netherlands?
immigration.services.0.faq.items.0.a: Yes. Partners of highly skilled migrants receive a residence permit with free access to the labour market. No separate work permit is needed.
immigration.services.0.faq.items.1.q: How long does the application take?
immigration.services.0.faq.items.1.a: Applications through a recognized sponsor run on the IND’s faster track, and in practice most cases move quickly. We confirm current IND timelines and fees during your intake instead of quoting numbers that go stale.
immigration.services.0.faq.items.2.q: Do I need to speak Dutch?
immigration.services.0.faq.items.2.a: No. There is no language requirement for this permit, and daily life in the international communities around Rotterdam and The Hague runs comfortably in English.
immigration.services.0.faq.items.3.q: Can my partner work in the Netherlands?
immigration.services.0.faq.items.3.a: Yes. Partners of highly skilled migrants receive a permit with free access to the labour market, which means no separate work permit and no employer sponsorship. Children are included in the same family application.

immigration.services.1.metaTitle: EU Blue Card Netherlands | Application Support for Expats
immigration.services.1.metaDescription: Apply for the EU Blue Card in the Netherlands with personal guidance. Degree recognition, employer coordination and a permit that travels with your European career.
immigration.services.1.intro.0: The EU Blue Card is the European work permit for higher educated professionals, and the Dutch version has become genuinely attractive. It gives you the right to live and work in the Netherlands, and it builds mobility rights across the EU that a national permit does not.
immigration.services.1.intro.1: Our reputation was built in the embassy world, and Blue Card files reward exactly that kind of precision: a correctly evaluated degree, a compliant contract and a clean submission. We make sure yours is all three.
immigration.services.1.cardText: The European work permit for higher educated professionals, with mobility across the EU.
immigration.services.1.explainer.title: What is the EU Blue Card?
immigration.services.1.explainer.text.0: The EU Blue Card is a European residence and work permit for university-educated professionals. Where the Dutch highly skilled migrant permit only asks about salary and a recognised sponsor, the Blue Card also asks for a completed higher education programme, and in return it gives you rights that reach beyond the Netherlands.
immigration.services.1.explainer.text.1: That is the real difference. A Blue Card builds towards mobility inside the European Union and towards EU long-term resident status, which the national permit does not. It is the better choice when the Netherlands is a chapter rather than the whole book.

immigration.services.1.included.blocks.0: We compare the Blue Card against the highly skilled migrant permit for your specific case, because for some profiles one is clearly better than the other.
immigration.services.1.included.blocks.1: Foreign diplomas usually need recognition in the Netherlands. We guide the credential evaluation so your qualification is accepted without back and forth.
immigration.services.1.included.blocks.2: Your contract must meet the current IND salary threshold and duration requirements. We review it before submission, not after a rejection.

immigration.services.1.conditions.title: Blue Card conditions
immigration.services.1.conditions.intro: The Blue Card is decided on three things: your qualification, your contract and your salary. This is where the lines sit.
A completed higher education programme of at least three years, or for ICT roles at least three years of relevant experience gained in the last seven.
Gross monthly salary from 5,942 euro, or 4,754 euro under the reduced criterion for recent graduates and shortage professions (2026, excluding holiday allowance).
An employment contract or binding job offer running for at least six months.
Foreign diplomas must be evaluated by IDW or Nuffic. Dutch qualifications need no evaluation.
Your employer does not need to be a recognised sponsor, which is the practical advantage over the highly skilled migrant permit.
Thresholds are indexed on 1 January and applied as at the filing date, not the contract date.
immigration.services.1.details.title: The Blue Card in practice
immigration.services.1.details.items.0.q: How does EU mobility actually work?
immigration.services.1.details.items.0.a: After twelve months of legal residence as a Blue Card holder you can move to another member state under a shortened procedure, and years spent in different member states count together towards EU long-term resident status. A Dutch highly skilled migrant permit gives you none of this.
immigration.services.1.details.items.1.q: Blue Card or highly skilled migrant?
immigration.services.1.details.items.1.a: If your employer is a recognised sponsor and you intend to build your career in the Netherlands, the highly skilled migrant permit is usually faster and simpler. If your employer is not recognised, or your career is likely to move across Europe, the Blue Card is the stronger instrument. You get the comparison in writing before you commit.
immigration.services.1.details.items.2.q: Can I qualify on experience instead of a degree?
immigration.services.1.details.items.2.a: Only in ICT. Managers and specialists in information and communication technology can qualify on at least three years of relevant experience obtained in the seven years before the application. Every other profession needs the diploma.
immigration.services.1.details.items.3.q: How long does diploma evaluation take?
immigration.services.1.details.items.3.a: IDW usually returns an evaluation in about four weeks, longer where an institution is slow to confirm authenticity. We start it in parallel with the rest of the file so it never becomes the bottleneck.
immigration.services.1.details.items.4.q: What does the Blue Card build towards?
immigration.services.1.details.items.4.a: Once you have five years of legal residence in the EU with at least two of them in the Netherlands, you can apply for EU long-term resident status here. That accumulation across borders is unique to this permit.
immigration.services.1.faq.title: Practical questions
immigration.services.1.faq.items.0.q: What salary do I need for the EU Blue Card?
immigration.services.1.faq.items.0.a: The threshold is set by the IND and adjusted each year, with a lower level for recent graduates. We check your offer against the current figures during intake rather than publishing numbers that expire.
immigration.services.1.faq.items.1.q: Blue Card or highly skilled migrant, which is better?
immigration.services.1.faq.items.1.a: It depends. The highly skilled migrant route is often faster if your employer is a recognized sponsor. The Blue Card wins on EU mobility and does not require sponsorship. We advise per case, honestly.
immigration.services.1.faq.items.2.a: Yes. Your partner and children can apply with you, and your partner may work in the Netherlands without a separate work permit.
immigration.services.1.faq.items.3.q: Does the 30 percent ruling count towards the salary threshold?
immigration.services.1.faq.items.3.a: No. The IND tests your gross salary before the ruling is applied. A contract that only reaches the threshold once the ruling is counted will be refused, and this is one of the most common reasons a Blue Card file fails.

immigration.services.2.metaTitle: Orientation Year Visa Netherlands | Zoekjaar for Graduates
immigration.services.2.metaDescription: Recent graduate or PhD? The Dutch orientation year visa gives you twelve months to live and work freely in the Netherlands. We handle the application and your landing.
immigration.services.2.intro.0: The orientation year, the zoekjaar, is one of the most generous permits in Europe. If you graduated recently from a Dutch institution or a highly ranked international university, it gives you twelve months to live in the Netherlands and work for any employer, no sponsorship required.
immigration.services.2.intro.1: The application itself is straightforward when done right, so our real value is what comes after: turning that year into a career and a home. We guide graduates from the first form to the first apartment, and stay close while you find your footing.
immigration.services.2.cardText: Twelve months to live and work freely in the Netherlands after your degree.
immigration.services.2.explainer.title: What is the orientation year?
immigration.services.2.explainer.text.0: The orientation year, zoekjaar in Dutch, is a one-year residence permit that lets recent graduates and researchers look for work in the Netherlands without an employer sponsoring them first. During that year you may work freely, with no work permit required from any employer.
immigration.services.2.explainer.text.1: It exists to solve a chicken-and-egg problem: employers want someone who can start, and permits usually need an employer. The orientation year removes that deadlock, and it comes with a lower salary threshold afterwards if you move onto a highly skilled migrant permit.

immigration.services.2.conditions.title: Who qualifies for the zoekjaar
immigration.services.2.conditions.intro: The orientation year is generous once you are inside it, and strict about who gets in. The window is the part people miss.
You must apply within three years of graduating, obtaining your PhD or completing your research.
Graduates of accredited Dutch bachelor, master and PhD programmes qualify on the Dutch degree alone.
International graduates need a degree from a university ranked in the top 200 of a recognised global ranking.
The permit runs for twelve months, cannot be extended, and can only be granted once.
You may work employed or self-employed for the whole year with no work permit and no salary threshold.
In the year that follows, the reduced highly skilled migrant criterion of 3,122 euro applies (2026).
immigration.services.2.details.title: Making the year count
immigration.services.2.details.items.0.q: What makes me easier to hire during the zoekjaar?
immigration.services.2.details.items.0.a: You have free access to the Dutch labour market. Your employer needs no work permit, no sponsorship and pays no IND fee, which removes the exact objection that blocks other non-EU candidates. Put it in your first line, because most Dutch employers do not know it.
immigration.services.2.details.items.1.q: What happens at the end of the twelve months?
immigration.services.2.details.items.1.a: You switch to another permit, most often the highly skilled migrant permit at the reduced criterion. The switch has to be filed before the orientation year expires, so we begin preparing it around month nine rather than month twelve.
immigration.services.2.details.items.2.q: Can I start a business during the year?
immigration.services.2.details.items.2.a: You can register at the KvK and work as a self-employed person for the duration. Converting to a permanent entrepreneurial basis afterwards is a separate application with its own test, so it is worth planning from the start.
immigration.services.2.details.items.3.a: Yes. Your partner can apply for a dependent permit for the same twelve months and also has free access to the labour market.
immigration.services.2.faq.title: Frequently asked
immigration.services.2.faq.items.0.q: Can I work during the orientation year?
immigration.services.2.faq.items.0.a: Yes, fully and freely. Any employer can hire you without a work permit or sponsorship during the twelve months.
immigration.services.2.faq.items.1.q: Do I need a job or income to apply?
immigration.services.2.faq.items.1.a: No job offer is required. You do need to show you can support yourself, and we walk you through what the IND accepts as proof.
immigration.services.2.faq.items.2.q: What happens when the year ends?
immigration.services.2.faq.items.2.a: Most graduates switch to a highly skilled migrant permit through their new employer, at a reduced salary threshold that makes hiring you easier. We plan that transition well before month twelve.

immigration.services.3.title: Partner Visa Netherlands
immigration.services.3.metaTitle: Partner Visa Netherlands | Bring Your Partner Home
immigration.services.3.metaDescription: Bring your partner to the Netherlands with confidence. We guide the full partner visa process, from income requirements to the civic integration exam and the embassy appointment.
immigration.services.3.intro.0: No application carries more weight than the one that brings the person you love to your doorstep. The Dutch partner visa is very doable, but it is unforgiving of small mistakes: an income document in the wrong format, a missed exam registration, a certificate without the right stamp, and you lose months.
immigration.services.3.intro.1: We treat these cases with the care they deserve. Johanna personally goes with clients to their appointments, from the municipality desk to the IND, so neither of you ever sits across from an official unprepared.
immigration.services.3.cardText: Careful, personal guidance for bringing your partner or spouse to the Netherlands.
immigration.services.3.explainer.title: What is a partner visa?
immigration.services.3.explainer.text.0: A partner visa is residence granted on the basis of your relationship rather than your job. One of you, the sponsor, already has the right to live in the Netherlands. The other applies to join them. Marriage is not required, but an unmarried relationship has to be evidenced as durable and exclusive.
immigration.services.3.explainer.text.1: The Dutch procedure tests three things: that the relationship is genuine, that the sponsor earns a stable and sufficient income, and that any civil documents from abroad are properly legalised and translated. Most refusals come from the third, not the first.

immigration.services.3.conditions.title: What has to be true
immigration.services.3.conditions.intro: Partner applications are refused on evidence far more often than on eligibility. These are the conditions, and the places files are usually lost.
The sponsor in the Netherlands must earn at least 2,523.96 euro gross per month including holiday allowance (2026, revised twice a year).
That income must be durable. A permanent contract clears it outright, a temporary one is judged on what remains.
The relationship must be exclusive, long-term and demonstrable. Marriage, registered partnership and documented unmarried relationships all qualify.
Both partners must be at least 21 years old.
Most partners must pass the basic civic integration exam abroad before an MVV can be issued.
Foreign birth, marriage and unmarried-status certificates usually need legalisation or an apostille plus a sworn translation.
immigration.services.3.details.title: The sensitive points we manage
immigration.services.3.details.items.0.a: A permanent contract clears it outright. On a temporary contract the IND asks whether the income will still be there for the next twelve months, and a contract with at least a year to run, or a three-year employment history, usually satisfies that. Self-employed sponsors are assessed on three years of accounts.
immigration.services.3.details.items.1.q: We are not married. Does that count against us?
immigration.services.3.details.items.1.a: No, but it raises the evidence bar. We build a relationship file: joint address history, shared finances, travel, photographs across years, communication records and statements from people who know you. This is where refused applications are lost, and where careful preparation wins them.
immigration.services.3.details.items.2.q: Who is exempt from the integration exam abroad?
immigration.services.3.details.items.2.a: Nationals of the EU, EEA, Switzerland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea and the United Kingdom, among a few others, plus applicants who cannot sit it for medical reasons or who hold a Dutch or Belgian qualification. Everyone else takes the exam at a Dutch embassy.
immigration.services.3.details.items.3.q: We were refused before. Can that be repaired?
immigration.services.3.details.items.3.a: Often, yes. A refusal is not a permanent bar, but the second file has to answer the exact ground of the first refusal rather than repeat the first attempt. Send us the decision letter and you will get an honest read on whether a fresh application or a formal objection is the better route.
immigration.services.3.faq.title: Couples ask us
immigration.services.3.faq.items.0.q: Can my partner work once they arrive?
immigration.services.3.faq.items.0.a: Yes. The partner residence permit comes with free access to the Dutch labour market, so they can take any job without a separate work permit.
immigration.services.3.faq.items.1.q: How much income do I need as a sponsor?
immigration.services.3.faq.items.1.a: The IND requires sustainable, independent income at a level it adjusts twice a year. We check your exact situation, including contracts and self-employment, during intake.
immigration.services.3.faq.items.2.q: We are not married. Is that a problem?
immigration.services.3.faq.items.2.a: No. The Netherlands recognizes durable relationships between unmarried partners. You will need to evidence the relationship, and we help you build that file convincingly.

immigration.services.4.title: Family Reunification Netherlands
immigration.services.4.metaTitle: Family Reunification Netherlands | Move as One Family
immigration.services.4.metaDescription: Family reunification in the Netherlands, handled with warmth and precision. Permits for spouses and children, school search and a soft landing for the whole family.
immigration.services.4.intro.0: A move only succeeds when the whole family arrives well. Family reunification lets your spouse and children join you in the Netherlands, and doing it properly means bundling permits, certificates from your home country and school planning into one coordinated operation.
immigration.services.4.intro.1: We run that operation for families around Rotterdam, Europoort and the wider industrial region, where international professionals arrive on contracts and their families follow. It is our home turf, and it shapes everything from which schools we recommend to which municipality desks we know by name.
immigration.services.4.cardText: Permits for your spouse and children, coordinated so the whole family lands together.
immigration.services.4.explainer.title: What is family reunification?
immigration.services.4.explainer.text.0: Family reunification, gezinshereniging in Dutch, is the route that brings a partner and children to live with someone who already holds residence in the Netherlands. It is a single legal framework covering the whole household rather than a separate procedure per person.
immigration.services.4.explainer.text.1: The IND assesses the sponsor as much as the applicants: a stable income at or above the statutory threshold, suitable housing, and civil status documents from the country of origin that survive legalisation. Children have their own evidence requirements around custody and parental consent.

immigration.services.4.conditions.title: Conditions for the family file
immigration.services.4.conditions.intro: One sponsor carries the whole family application. Everything below is tested against that person, and against paperwork issued in countries you have already left.
The main permit holder acts as sponsor and must hold a valid residence permit on a non-temporary basis.
Income of at least 2,523.96 euro gross per month including holiday allowance, assessed as durable (2026 figure).
Children must be minors, unmarried, and must have belonged to the family before the move to the Netherlands.
Where one parent remains abroad, written consent from that parent is required before a child can move.
Certificates from most countries need legalisation or an apostille and a sworn translation into Dutch, English, French or German.
Applications filed together with the main applicant are decided faster than applications filed afterwards.
immigration.services.4.details.title: How family files really run
immigration.services.4.details.items.0.q: Should we apply together or follow later?
immigration.services.4.details.items.0.a: Together whenever it is possible. A simultaneous family application is decided alongside the main file, lands on one timeline and avoids a second income test. Following later is entirely workable, it simply costs an extra procedure and several months apart.
immigration.services.4.details.items.1.a: Between two weeks and six months depending on the country, because in many places the chain runs through the local ministry of foreign affairs and then the Dutch embassy. This is the single most common cause of delay in family files, which is why we start it before anything else.
immigration.services.4.details.items.2.q: Can our children start school straight away?
immigration.services.4.details.items.2.a: Yes. Children in the Netherlands have both the right and the obligation to attend school regardless of permit status, and international schools and newcomer classes usually admit them within weeks. We run the school search alongside the permit rather than after it.
immigration.services.4.details.items.3.q: What if a child turns eighteen during the procedure?
immigration.services.4.details.items.3.a: The IND assesses age at the moment of submission, so a child who was a minor when the application was filed does not lose eligibility by having a birthday while it is pending. It is precisely why we file early rather than file perfectly.
immigration.services.4.faq.title: What families want to know
immigration.services.4.faq.items.0.q: Can my spouse work in the Netherlands?
immigration.services.4.faq.items.0.a: In most cases yes. Spouses of highly skilled migrants and most permit holders receive free access to the labour market on arrival.
immigration.services.4.faq.items.1.q: Will my children need to learn Dutch?
immigration.services.4.faq.items.1.a: Not necessarily. The Rotterdam and The Hague regions have strong international and bilingual schools. Younger children often pick up Dutch quickly in local schools, and we advise per child, not per brochure.
immigration.services.4.faq.items.2.q: Can we all apply at the same time?
immigration.services.4.faq.items.2.a: Yes, and you usually should. Bundled applications keep the family on one timeline and one decision moment. We structure it that way whenever possible.

immigration.services.5.metaDescription: The startup visa Netherlands gives non-EU founders a one-year residence permit to build an innovative company with a recognised facilitator. Requirements, process and fees.
immigration.services.5.intro.0: The startup visa Netherlands is designed for international entrepreneurs who want to develop an innovative business here. It grants a one-year startup phase in which you build the company alongside a recognised startup facilitator, inside an ecosystem with real access to investors, incubators and international markets.
immigration.services.5.intro.1: We guide the whole arc, not only the permit: the facilitator match, the startup plan the IND wants to read, and the practical side of arriving, from company registration to a place to live.
immigration.services.5.cardText: A one-year founder permit to build your innovative company in the Dutch ecosystem.
immigration.services.5.explainer.title: What is the startup visa?
immigration.services.5.explainer.text.0: The startup visa is a one-year residence permit for entrepreneurs building an innovative business in the Netherlands. It exists because a genuinely new company rarely has the revenue or the track record that the ordinary self-employed permit demands on day one.
immigration.services.5.explainer.text.1: Its defining feature is the facilitator: an experienced mentor approved by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency who guides your company through its first year. You are assessed on the innovation in the plan and on that partnership, not on turnover. The year is a runway to the self-employed permit, and preparing that next step early is the difference between continuing and starting again.

immigration.services.6.metaDescription: The DAFT visa Netherlands lets US citizens live and work here as entrepreneurs with a 4,500 euro business investment. Requirements, working method and professional fees.
immigration.services.6.intro.0: The DAFT visa Netherlands, granted under the Dutch American Friendship Treaty, is the most accessible immigration route for US citizens who want to run their own business here. Because of the treaty between the Netherlands and the United States, American entrepreneurs qualify under more flexible conditions than the standard entrepreneur permit.
immigration.services.6.intro.1: It is the route freelancers, consultants and small business owners use most. Alongside the immigration file we handle the practical side of arriving: company registration, housing, and residence for the family coming with you.
immigration.services.6.cardText: The treaty route that lets Americans live and work in the Netherlands as entrepreneurs.
immigration.services.6.explainer.title: What is the DAFT permit?
immigration.services.6.explainer.text.0: The DAFT permit comes from the Dutch American Friendship Treaty, a 1956 agreement that gives United States citizens a uniquely accessible route to self-employment in the Netherlands. It is open only to Americans, and it is by some distance the easiest entrepreneurial permit the country offers.
immigration.services.6.explainer.text.1: The treaty replaces the points system that other nationalities face with one straightforward test: register a genuine Dutch business and keep a defined minimum investment in the company’s equity. There is no innovation requirement, no facilitator and no scoring of your business plan. Maintaining the investment is what keeps the permit alive at renewal.

immigration.services.6.details.title: Detail worth reading before you apply
immigration.services.6.details.items.0.q: What exactly is the DAFT residence permit?
immigration.services.6.details.items.0.a: It allows US citizens to live in the Netherlands while operating their own business here. Unlike the regular entrepreneur residence permit, the DAFT route does not require a points-based economic assessment of the business plan. The primary requirement is the minimum business investment.
immigration.services.6.details.items.1.a: Both can satisfy the treaty. A sole proprietorship is lighter and cheaper to run; a BV limits liability and suits growth and investors. The choice changes how the investment is evidenced and how you are taxed, so we advise on your numbers rather than a rule of thumb.
immigration.services.6.details.items.2.q: What does maintaining the investment mean in practice?
immigration.services.6.details.items.2.a: The capital has to remain in the business, visible on the balance sheet, not withdrawn once the permit is granted. Your bookkeeping is the proof at renewal, which is why we introduce clients to accountants who know the treaty well.
immigration.services.6.faq.title: Americans ask us
immigration.services.6.faq.items.0.q: Can my spouse work in the Netherlands under DAFT?
immigration.services.6.faq.items.0.a: Yes. Your spouse receives a residence permit with free access to the labour market, so they can take a job or start their own venture.
immigration.services.6.faq.items.1.q: Do I need clients or revenue before applying?
immigration.services.6.faq.items.1.a: No revenue threshold applies at the start. You need the investment, a registered business and the intent to actually run it. By renewal time your accounts should show a living business.
immigration.services.6.faq.items.2.q: Does DAFT lead to permanent residence?
immigration.services.6.faq.items.2.a: It can. After five years of continuous legal residence you may generally apply for permanent residence or naturalisation, subject to the integration requirements. Many of our DAFT clients follow that path.

immigration.services.7.metaDescription: Short-stay business Schengen visas for the Netherlands, prepared properly. Invitation letters, embassy files and support for delegations visiting Dutch partners.
immigration.services.7.intro.0: Not every journey to the Netherlands is a move. Deals get signed, ports get inspected, partnerships get built, and for many nationalities that requires a short-stay Schengen visa: up to 90 days within any 180-day period, for business purposes.
immigration.services.7.intro.1: These files live and die at the consulate, and that is a world we know intimately. Our reputation was built in the embassy world, which means we know what a convincing business file looks like from the other side of the counter.
immigration.services.7.cardText: Short-stay visas for meetings, negotiations and site visits in the Netherlands.
immigration.services.7.explainer.title: What is a business visa?
immigration.services.7.explainer.text.0: A business visa is a short-stay Schengen visa, type C, for meetings, negotiations, conferences and site visits. It allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area, and it does not permit you to take up employment in the Netherlands.
immigration.services.7.explainer.text.1: Nationals of many countries need one before travelling; others are visa-exempt for short stays. The application is decided by the consulate on the strength of the invitation, your travel history, insurance and evidence that you will return, which is why the supporting file matters more than the form.

immigration.services.7.conditions.title: What this visa does and does not allow
immigration.services.7.conditions.intro: The limits matter more than the requirements here, because using this visa for the wrong activity puts both the traveller and the Dutch host at risk.
A maximum of ninety days of stay within any one hundred and eighty day period across the Schengen area.
Meetings, negotiations, training, trade fairs and site visits are permitted. Paid work in the Netherlands is not.
A formal invitation from the Dutch host company is required, and the host may be asked to accept liability for costs.
Travel medical insurance with at least 30,000 euro of cover, valid throughout Schengen, is mandatory.
Proof of accommodation, return travel and sufficient means for the stay must be provided.
File at the Dutch mission only if the Netherlands is your main destination, otherwise the application belongs to the country where you spend most time.
immigration.services.7.details.title: Getting a stronger decision
immigration.services.7.details.items.0.a: Almost always for one of three reasons: the purpose of travel is not credible in the documents, the applicant cannot show sufficient ties to their home country, or earlier Schengen travel was used improperly. All three are file problems, and all three can be addressed before submission.
immigration.services.7.details.items.1.q: How do we get a multi-entry visa?
immigration.services.7.details.items.1.a: Multi-entry visas of one to five years go to applicants with a clean Schengen travel history and a demonstrable ongoing business relationship. We structure the file so the recurring pattern is visible in the evidence rather than requested as a favour.
immigration.services.7.details.items.2.q: How far ahead should we apply?
immigration.services.7.details.items.2.a: Applications can be filed up to six months before travel and no later than fifteen days before. Consulate appointment availability is the real constraint, and in busy regions and peak season slots can be six weeks out. Tell us the date early.
immigration.services.7.details.items.3.q: Our specialist needs to work on site. Is this the right visa?
immigration.services.7.details.items.3.a: No. Installing equipment, delivering a project or performing services for a Dutch client is work, and needs a work-based permit or a notification under the posted workers rules. Using a business visa for it exposes your company and your employee. We will tell you which instrument actually applies.
immigration.services.7.faq.title: Before you book flights
immigration.services.7.faq.items.0.a: Consulate lead times vary sharply by country and season. As a rule, start as soon as the trip is certain. We confirm current appointment availability for your consulate when you contact us.
immigration.services.7.faq.items.1.q: Can I visit other Schengen countries on this visa?
immigration.services.7.faq.items.1.a: Yes. A Schengen visa allows travel throughout the Schengen area, but you should apply through the Netherlands when it is your main destination.
immigration.services.7.faq.items.2.q: What if a previous application was refused?
immigration.services.7.faq.items.2.a: A refusal is not the end. We analyse the stated grounds, repair the weak points in the file and structure the reapplication accordingly.
immigration.services.7.cta.title: A meeting in the Netherlands to arrange?
immigration.services.7.cta.text: Send us the travel dates and the purpose. We will tell you exactly what the file needs and how fast it can move.

immigration.services.8.metaTitle: Residence Permit Netherlands for Expats | Renewals & Advice
immigration.services.8.metaDescription: Residence permits in the Netherlands explained and handled: first applications, renewals, changes of purpose and the road to permanent residence, with personal guidance.
immigration.services.8.intro.0: Every expat life in the Netherlands runs on a residence permit, and the permit itself has a life: it gets granted, renewed, changed when your situation changes, and eventually upgraded to permanent residence. Miss a renewal window or change jobs without checking the consequences, and years of careful building can wobble.
immigration.services.8.intro.1: We act as the immigration desk our clients never have to think about. We track the dates, prepare the files, and Johanna accompanies clients to their IND appointments in person, so a summons never feels like a threat.
immigration.services.8.cardText: First permits, renewals, changes and the road to permanent residence, all under one roof.
immigration.services.8.explainer.title: What is a Dutch residence permit?
immigration.services.8.explainer.text.0: A residence permit, verblijfsvergunning in Dutch, is the document that makes your stay in the Netherlands lawful beyond 90 days. It is issued by the IND, it always states a purpose of stay such as work, family or study, and the rights that come with it follow that purpose rather than the card itself.
immigration.services.8.explainer.text.1: Permits are either temporary or permanent. What matters most for the long term is which purpose you hold and for how long, because continuous lawful residence is what eventually opens permanent residence and naturalisation. Changing purpose is possible, but the timing decides whether your accrued years survive the change.

immigration.services.8.forWho.items.0: Your permit is approaching its expiry date
immigration.services.8.forWho.items.1: Your situation changed: new employer, new relationship, a divorce, a new company

immigration.services.8.included.blocks.0: One review of your current permit, its conditions and its expiry, with a clear calendar of what must happen when.
immigration.services.8.included.blocks.1: We prepare renewal applications early and completely, so continuity of your residence rights is never in question.
immigration.services.8.included.blocks.2: From graduate to employee, from partner to independent, from startup to self-employed. We manage the switch so the new basis is secured before the old one ends.
immigration.services.8.included.blocks.3: After five years of legal residence you may qualify for a permanent permit or EU long-term residence, usually including a civic integration requirement. We assess your readiness and build the application.
immigration.services.8.process.title: How we work
immigration.services.8.process.steps.0.t: We audit your current status and flag every date and condition that matters.
immigration.services.8.process.steps.1.t: The right application, assembled ahead of the deadline with room to spare.

immigration.services.8.fees.includes.3: Follow-up until the decision, including renewals where relevant
immigration.services.8.note: Fees and decision periods differ per permit type and change over time, so we confirm the current IND figures during your intake rather than printing them here.
immigration.services.8.conditions.title: Timing and thresholds
immigration.services.8.conditions.intro: Almost every permit problem we repair began as a date that passed quietly. These are the ones that matter.
File a renewal at least three months before expiry. Your right to live and work continues while a timely renewal is pending.
A change of employer, purpose or relationship needs a new application, and in most cases you may not begin the new activity before approval.
Permanent residence requires five years of uninterrupted legal residence on a non-temporary basis.
Study permits and orientation year permits do not count towards those five years.
Civic integration at level A2, or a formal exemption, is required for permanent residence and for naturalisation.
Absences of more than six consecutive months, or more than four months a year across the period, break the continuity.
immigration.services.8.details.title: The questions we are asked most
immigration.services.8.details.items.0.a: Permanent residence secures your right to live and work here indefinitely and survives a change of job. Nationality adds a Dutch passport, EU citizenship and the vote, needs the same five years plus integration, and usually requires you to give up your existing nationality. Many clients take permanent residence first and decide about naturalisation later.
immigration.services.8.details.items.1.q: My permit expires soon and I have no new job.
immigration.services.8.details.items.1.a: Highly skilled migrants have a three-month search period after employment ends, during which residence continues while you find a new recognised sponsor. Act inside that window. Once it closes the position becomes much harder to repair.
immigration.services.8.details.items.2.q: I am getting divorced. Do I lose my residence?
immigration.services.8.details.items.2.a: Not necessarily. Depending on how long you have held a dependent permit and on your own circumstances, a change of purpose to independent residence is often possible. This is time sensitive, and the earlier you speak to us the more routes stay open.
immigration.services.8.details.items.3.q: Can I hold EU long-term resident status as well?
immigration.services.8.details.items.3.a: Yes, and it is often the better combination. The EU long-term resident permit adds mobility rights towards other member states that Dutch permanent residence does not carry, and both can be applied for at the same time.
immigration.services.8.faq.title: Residence questions
immigration.services.8.faq.items.0.q: When should I start my renewal?
immigration.services.8.faq.items.0.a: The IND lets you apply in the months before expiry, and earlier is almost always better. We typically start preparing well before the window opens so submission day is a formality.
immigration.services.8.faq.items.1.q: Do I need to speak Dutch for permanent residence?
immigration.services.8.faq.items.1.a: Usually yes. Permanent residence generally requires passing civic integration exams, with exemptions in specific cases. We assess which requirements apply to you and how to prepare.
immigration.services.8.faq.items.2.q: What happens to my permit if I lose my job?
immigration.services.8.faq.items.2.a: It depends on your permit type. Highly skilled migrants, for example, get a search period to find a new sponsor. The key is acting immediately, so call us the week it happens, not the month after.

immigration.services.8.cta.text: Send us a photo of your permit card and your situation in three sentences. We will tell you what needs attention and when.

Deposits above the legal norm, service costs that quietly cover things they should not, temporary contracts dressed up as permanent ones, penalty clauses that would never survive a judge. housing.services.3.intro.1: We review your contract line by line and give you a plain-English summary of what you are agreeing to, what is standard, what is negotiable and what is simply not allowed under Dutch tenancy law. housing.services.3.conditions.title: What we check, and what we cannot
housing.services.3.conditions.intro: Dutch tenancy law protects you more than most newcomers realise. Knowing which protections apply is the whole game.
housing.services.3.conditions.items.0: Deposits are capped at two months of basic rent for contracts signed since 1 July 2023.
housing.services.3.conditions.items.1: Since 1 July 2024 most new residential leases must be indefinite, with fixed-term contracts permitted only in defined situations.
housing.services.3.conditions.items.2: Service charges must be specified and settled annually against actual costs. A single all-in figure is not permitted for most rentals.
housing.services.3.conditions.items.3: Agency fees may not be charged to the tenant where the agent acts for the landlord.
housing.services.3.conditions.items.4: A rent above the legally permitted level under the points system can be challenged at the Huurcommissie, in most cases within six months of the start of the lease.
housing.services.3.conditions.items.5: We review contracts and explain your position. We are relocation consultants, not a law firm, and for proceedings we refer you to a Dutch housing lawyer we trust.
housing.services.3.details.title: Clauses that cost money later
housing.services.3.details.items.0.q: Which clauses do you look for first?
housing.services.3.details.items.0.a: Break options and diplomatic clauses, who pays for minor repairs, whether the deposit is returnable within a fixed period, indexation formulas that outrun inflation, restrictions on registering at the address, service charge estimates set unrealistically low, and penalties for early termination.
housing.services.3.details.items.1.q: Can I register at this address?
housing.services.3.details.items.1.a: This is the clause that matters most and the one most often quietly excluded. Without registration there is no BSN, no health insurance, no bank account and no permit correspondence. If the contract forbids it or stays silent, we raise it before you sign rather than after.
housing.services.3.details.items.2.q: What if the rent is too high for the property?
housing.services.3.details.items.2.a: The Dutch points system sets a maximum legal rent for most homes based on size, energy label, fittings and location. Where a rent exceeds it the Huurcommissie can reduce it, usually on an application made within six months of the start of the lease. We flag this during review while the window is still open.
housing.services.3.details.items.3.a: Normally within one business day, and the same day when you are under pressure to sign. A landlord who insists you sign within the hour is applying a tactic, not describing a deadline.
housing.services.3.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
housing.services.3.faq.items.0.q: How high can a deposit legally be?
housing.services.3.faq.items.0.a: For most contracts signed today the deposit is capped at twice the basic monthly rent. If a landlord asks for more, that is a red flag we will address before you pay a cent.
housing.services.3.faq.items.1.q: My contract forbids registering at the address. Is that allowed?
housing.services.3.faq.items.1.a: No. If you legally live there, you are entitled to register with the municipality, and a clause forbidding it is a warning sign about the landlord. We treat this as a serious issue, since registration underpins your BSN and insurance.
housing.services.3.faq.items.2.q: What does furnished mean for my contract and my rent?
housing.services.3.faq.items.2.a: Furniture is charged through service costs, which must reflect the real value of what is provided. We check that an aging sofa is not costing you a premium every month, and that the inventory list matches what is actually in the home.

housing.services.4.conditions.title: Short stay, in practice
housing.services.4.conditions.intro: A temporary base is a bridge, and bridges are worth choosing carefully. These are the conditions that decide whether yours works.
housing.services.4.conditions.items.0: Short-stay rentals typically run from one to six months and cost more per month than a standard lease, often thirty to fifty percent more.
housing.services.4.conditions.items.1: Registration at the address is only possible where both the landlord and the municipality permit it, and many short-stay addresses do not.
housing.services.4.conditions.items.2: Without registration there is no BSN, which delays health insurance, banking and in some cases salary payment.
housing.services.4.conditions.items.3: Most short-stay properties are furnished with utilities and internet included, but cleaning and linen often are not.
housing.services.4.conditions.items.4: Minimum stays, cancellation terms and deposits vary widely between operators and are rarely negotiable.
housing.services.4.conditions.items.5: We place clients only in properties we would use ourselves, and decline operators whose contracts we do not trust.
housing.services.4.details.title: Using the bridge properly
housing.services.4.details.items.0.q: Can I register at a short-stay address?
housing.services.4.details.items.0.a: Sometimes, and it changes everything. We filter for registration-friendly properties from the start, because a base that allows registration lets your BSN, insurance and salary run from week one instead of month three. Where registration is impossible we plan around it deliberately rather than discover it late.
housing.services.4.details.items.1.q: How long should I book for?
housing.services.4.details.items.1.a: Six to ten weeks suits most arrivals. It gives the permanent search room to breathe without paying the short-stay premium longer than necessary, and most operators will extend if the search runs on.
housing.services.4.details.items.2.a: For under three weeks, often yes. Beyond that, short-stay apartments win on both cost and sanity, particularly for families. The tipping point usually falls around the third week.
housing.services.4.details.items.3.q: What about belongings arriving from abroad?
housing.services.4.details.items.3.a: Short-stay contracts rarely include storage. We coordinate your shipment against the permanent address rather than the temporary one, and arrange storage in the region when the timings will not meet.
housing.services.4.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
housing.services.4.faq.items.0.q: Can I register for my BSN at a temporary address?
housing.services.4.faq.items.0.a: At many short-stay addresses yes, and we treat it as a priority filter when you need registration for your BSN, insurance or bank account. We confirm the registration policy with each provider before you book.
housing.services.4.faq.items.1.a: Almost always fully furnished, including linen, kitchenware, internet and utilities in one price. That premium is exactly what you are paying for: walking in with a suitcase and living normally that same night.
housing.services.4.faq.items.2.q: What if my pet is arriving with me?
housing.services.4.faq.items.2.a: Pet-friendly short-stay housing exists but is scarce, so tell us early. We approach pet-tolerant providers directly rather than gambling on a booking platform checkbox.

housing.services.5.conditions.title: What we can and cannot do
housing.services.5.conditions.intro: Most tenancy disputes are won by writing the right thing in the right language at the right moment. That is the work.
housing.services.5.conditions.items.0: We correspond with landlords and agents in Dutch, in your name, with you copied on everything that goes out.
housing.services.5.conditions.items.1: Repairs affecting safety, heating or water must be reported to the landlord first. A landlord who then fails to act can be taken to the Huurcommissie.
housing.services.5.conditions.items.2: Deposits must be returned within a reasonable period after the final inspection, and any deduction must be itemised and evidenced.
housing.services.5.conditions.items.3: Normal wear and tear may not be deducted from your deposit. Actual damage may.
housing.services.5.conditions.items.4: For disputes about rent level, service charges and maintenance, the Huurcommissie is usually far faster and cheaper than court.
housing.services.5.conditions.items.5: We are not a law firm. Where a dispute needs legal proceedings we hand over to a Dutch housing lawyer and stay on as your interpreter.
housing.services.5.details.title: The disputes we handle most
housing.services.5.details.items.0.q: My landlord is withholding the deposit.
housing.services.5.details.items.0.a: The most common dispute and usually the most winnable. We request an itemised statement with evidence, separate normal wear from actual damage, set the check-in report against the check-out, and give a formal deadline in Dutch. Most deposits come back at that stage without any proceedings at all.
housing.services.5.details.items.1.a: We report formally and in writing, which starts the clock legally rather than socially. If nothing happens, the Huurcommissie can order a temporary rent reduction until the repair is made, and the prospect of that usually produces a plumber.
housing.services.5.details.items.2.q: My service charges jumped without explanation.
housing.services.5.details.items.2.a: Landlords must provide an annual settlement showing actual costs against what you paid. We request it, check it against meter readings and challenge the parts that cannot be evidenced.
housing.services.5.details.items.3.a: Most indefinite contracts allow a tenant to terminate on one month's notice, whatever is said at the door. We check the clause, serve notice correctly and manage the final inspection so the deposit comes back intact.
housing.services.5.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
housing.services.5.faq.items.0.q: My landlord will not register my rental defects. What now?
housing.services.5.faq.items.0.a: Defects should be reported in writing with photos and a reasonable deadline. We draft that notice for you in Dutch, and if the landlord stays silent we escalate along the route the law provides, step by documented step.
housing.services.5.faq.items.1.q: How long can a landlord hold my deposit after I move out?
housing.services.5.faq.items.1.a: A deposit should normally be settled within a few weeks of the final inspection, with any deductions itemized and justified. Vague deductions for normal wear and tear do not hold up, and we challenge them.
housing.services.5.faq.items.2.q: Can my landlord stop me from keeping a pet?
housing.services.5.faq.items.2.a: A blanket ban is not automatically enforceable; much depends on the contract, the type of home and the nuisance involved. Before you rehome anything or sign anything, let us read what your contract really says.

relocation.services.0.details.title: Where BSN files go wrong
relocation.services.0.details.items.0.q: Why is legalisation such a problem?
relocation.services.0.details.items.0.a: A certificate that has not been legalised in the country of issue cannot be accepted, and the chain often runs through a local ministry and then a Dutch embassy. It can take weeks or months, and it cannot be started once you are already here. This is the single most common reason an arrival stalls, and it is the first thing we check.
relocation.services.0.details.items.1.q: Can I get a BSN without a Dutch address?
relocation.services.0.details.items.1.a: Yes, through the RNI register for non-residents, available at nineteen designated municipalities. It gives you a BSN so payroll and banking can start, but it is not residential registration, and you still register properly once you have your address.
relocation.services.0.details.items.2.q: What happens straight after the appointment?
relocation.services.0.details.items.2.a: Your BSN is usually issued on the spot or within a few days. It then unlocks the DigiD application, health insurance enrolment, a Dutch bank account and correct payroll. We work through that sequence with you rather than leaving you with a number and a list.
relocation.services.0.details.items.3.q: Do you come to the appointment with me?

relocation.services.1.metaDescription: Register with your Dutch municipality without stress. Document preparation, appointment booking and personal guidance through the gemeente process.
relocation.services.1.intro.0: Every resident of the Netherlands must be registered with their gemeente, the municipality, and that registration follows you everywhere: taxes, benefits, voting, parking permits, school places. Get it wrong, or let it lapse after a move, and small administrative errors quietly grow into real problems.
relocation.services.1.intro.1: We handle the whole relationship with your municipality. First registration when you arrive, re-registration when you move within the Netherlands, deregistration if you leave, and corrections when the records do not match reality. relocation.services.1.explainer.title: What is municipality registration?
relocation.services.1.explainer.text.0: Municipality registration enters you in the Basisregistratie Personen, the BRP, which is the Dutch population register. It records who you are and where you live, and it is what produces your BSN. Every level of Dutch administration reads from it.
relocation.services.1.explainer.text.1: It is a legal obligation with a deadline rather than an optional formality. You register at the gemeente of the address where you actually live, and you need the landlord’s permission for that address, which is the point where registrations most often fail.

relocation.services.1.conditions.title: Rules that catch people out
relocation.services.1.conditions.intro: The gemeente record follows you through every institution in the country, so an error here reappears everywhere.
relocation.services.1.conditions.items.0: First registration must be made within five days of arrival, and a move within the Netherlands within five days of moving.
relocation.services.1.conditions.items.1: A change of address must be reported to the new municipality, not the old one.
relocation.services.1.conditions.items.2: Registration requires the landlord's permission for the address. Registering where it is forbidden puts your tenancy at risk.
relocation.services.1.conditions.items.3: Your marital status, name spelling and place of birth are taken from legalised certificates, and correcting them later is far harder than getting them right once.
relocation.services.1.conditions.items.4: Leaving the Netherlands for more than eight months in a year requires deregistration, which affects insurance, benefits and permits.
relocation.services.1.conditions.items.5: Non-EU nationals normally collect their residence document from the IND, not the municipality. The two appointments are separate.
relocation.services.1.details.title: Getting the record right
relocation.services.1.details.items.0.q: Why does the spelling of my name matter so much?
relocation.services.1.details.items.0.a: The BRP record feeds your bank, your employer, the tax office, your insurer and the IND. A transliteration that differs from your passport by one letter produces mismatches that surface months later at the worst moment. We check the entry against your passport before the official saves it.
relocation.services.1.details.items.1.q: Can you correct a registration that is already wrong?
relocation.services.1.details.items.1.a: Usually yes, with the right supporting documents and a formal correction request. Errors in date of birth, marital status and previous nationality are the ones we repair most, and they are worth repairing rather than living with.
relocation.services.1.details.items.2.q: What if my landlord will not allow registration?
relocation.services.1.details.items.2.a: Then the address is a problem, not an inconvenience. We check registration permission before you sign a contract, and where a landlord refuses after the fact we take up the correspondence, because in most residential situations the refusal has no legal basis.
relocation.services.1.details.items.3.q: Do I have to deregister when I leave?
relocation.services.1.details.items.3.a: Yes, if you are leaving for more than eight months in a twelve month period. Failing to deregister leaves you liable for Dutch health insurance premiums and local taxes long after you have gone. We handle the exit as carefully as the arrival.
relocation.services.1.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
relocation.services.1.faq.items.0.q: What if my landlord has not given permission to register?
relocation.services.1.faq.items.0.a: You have the right to register where you actually live, and a landlord cannot lawfully forbid it. We approach the landlord first to resolve it amicably, and if needed we guide you through the municipality’s address investigation route.
relocation.services.1.faq.items.1.q: I moved within the Netherlands. Do I really need to re-register?
relocation.services.1.faq.items.1.a: Yes, within five days of moving, and it is not a formality. Your health insurer, tax office and employer all read from that record. We file the change online or at the desk and confirm it processed.
relocation.services.1.faq.items.2.q: Do my children need to come to the appointment?
relocation.services.1.faq.items.2.a: For a first registration, municipalities generally want to see every family member in person, children included. We plan one efficient family appointment so you are not returning three times.

relocation.services.2.conditions.title: How the Dutch system works
relocation.services.2.conditions.intro: Dutch health insurance is compulsory, private and time bound. Getting the timing wrong is expensive in a way that surprises most arrivals.
relocation.services.2.conditions.items.0: Anyone who lives or works in the Netherlands must take out Dutch basic health insurance within four months of registration.
relocation.services.2.conditions.items.1: Cover is backdated to your first day of residence, so a late enrolment produces a bill for the intervening months, plus a fine.
relocation.services.2.conditions.items.2: The basic package is set by government and identical at every insurer. Only price, service and supplementary cover differ.
relocation.services.2.conditions.items.3: There is a compulsory annual excess set by government, which you pay before most care is reimbursed. The GP is exempt from it.
relocation.services.2.conditions.items.4: You cannot see a specialist without a referral from your registered GP, except in emergencies.
relocation.services.2.conditions.items.5: Low and middle incomes may qualify for zorgtoeslag, a monthly healthcare allowance from the tax office.
relocation.services.2.details.title: Choosing well, not just quickly
relocation.services.2.details.items.0.q: Which supplementary cover is actually worth it?
relocation.services.2.details.items.0.a: Dental for adults, physiotherapy beyond the statutory minimum, and cover for care abroad are the three that repay themselves for most of our clients. Children are covered free on a parent's policy, including dental. Almost everything else is a personal calculation, and we do it with you rather than for you.
relocation.services.2.details.items.1.q: Why can I not find a GP?
relocation.services.2.details.items.1.a: Practices in Rotterdam and the larger cities regularly close their lists, and registration is required before you need care rather than at the moment you need it. We start the GP search in your first week, and we know which practices in the region are still accepting patients.
relocation.services.2.details.items.2.q: I have the 30 percent ruling. Does anything change?
relocation.services.2.details.items.2.a: Your insurance obligation does not change. What can change is your entitlement to zorgtoeslag, since the allowance is means tested on taxable income. We check it rather than assume it.
relocation.services.2.details.items.3.q: What if I only work here part of the year?
relocation.services.2.details.items.3.a: Cross-border and rotational situations are genuinely complicated, and getting them wrong means either double premiums or no cover at all. Offshore workers, posted employees and people with an employer in another EU state each fall under different rules, and we work through yours specifically.
relocation.services.2.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
relocation.services.2.faq.items.0.q: I have travel or international insurance. Is that enough?
relocation.services.2.faq.items.0.a: Usually not. Once you live or work here and are covered by the Dutch system, the basic Dutch policy is legally required regardless of other coverage. We check your specific situation, including exceptions for certain postings and students.
relocation.services.2.faq.items.1.q: Why do I need a GP before I am even sick?
relocation.services.2.faq.items.1.a: The huisarts is the gateway to all Dutch healthcare; hospitals expect a referral. Practices near you can have closed patient lists, so registering early, while you are healthy, is the single best healthcare decision a newcomer makes.
relocation.services.2.faq.items.2.q: What happens if a health question comes up outside office hours?
relocation.services.2.faq.items.2.a: The Netherlands has an after-hours GP service, the huisartsenpost, for urgent cases. And our clients can always message us on the personal WhatsApp line at any hour; we have talked more than one worried parent through their first Dutch night-time fever.

relocation.services.3.conditions.title: What families need to know first
relocation.services.3.conditions.intro: School places, not housing, are usually the real constraint on when a family can move. Plan this before anything else.
relocation.services.3.conditions.items.0: Education is compulsory from age five, and most children start at four.
relocation.services.3.conditions.items.1: International schools in the Rotterdam region have limited places and waiting lists, and popular year groups fill a year ahead.
relocation.services.3.conditions.items.2: Dutch international schools fall into two categories: subsidised Dutch international schools, which are far cheaper but require a demonstrable international background, and private international schools.
relocation.services.3.conditions.items.3: Children who do not yet speak Dutch usually spend a year in a nieuwkomersklas before entering mainstream Dutch education.
relocation.services.3.conditions.items.4: Enrolment normally requires proof of address and a BSN, which links the school timeline to the housing and registration timeline.
relocation.services.3.conditions.items.5: We advise on schools and manage the process. We cannot create a place where a school has none.
relocation.services.3.details.title: Choosing the right education
relocation.services.3.details.items.0.a: It turns on how long you intend to stay. Under three years, an international school protects continuity and the curriculum your child will return to. Beyond five, a Dutch school gives them the language, the friendships and a far easier adolescence. The years in between are a real decision, and we talk it through properly rather than pushing the expensive option.
relocation.services.3.details.items.1.a: Six to nine months before the move for international schools, and three months for Dutch schools. Where you are already inside that window we go directly to the schools that still have movement, which is a different list from the one you will find online.
relocation.services.3.details.items.2.a: Subsidised Dutch international schools are a few thousand euro a year. Private international schools in the region run considerably higher, and fees, registration and materials are usually billed separately. We set out the real annual figure per school on your shortlist so there are no surprises in month two.
relocation.services.3.details.items.3.q: Will my child cope with Dutch?
relocation.services.3.details.items.3.a: Younger children almost always do, and quickly. The nieuwkomersklas exists precisely for this, and a year in it typically brings a child to the point where mainstream education works. For teenagers approaching exams the calculation is different, and we are candid about that.
relocation.services.3.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
relocation.services.3.faq.items.0.q: Should we choose international or Dutch education?
relocation.services.3.faq.items.0.a: For postings under about three years, international schools offer continuity. For families staying longer, Dutch schools with a newcomer program often integrate children faster and cost far less. We help you decide based on your plans, not a general rule.
relocation.services.3.faq.items.1.q: My child does not speak Dutch. How do Dutch schools handle that?
relocation.services.3.faq.items.1.a: Many regions have dedicated newcomer classes where children get intensive Dutch for around a year before joining regular classes. Placement depends on age and region, and we find the actual options near your home.
relocation.services.3.faq.items.2.q: How bad are the waiting lists really?
relocation.services.3.faq.items.2.a: It varies enormously by city and school. Popular international schools can have long lists while an equally strong school nearby has places. Applying early and to the right mix of schools is most of the battle, and that is what we manage.

relocation.services.4.conditions.title: The order things have to happen in
relocation.services.4.conditions.intro: Dutch administration is a chain. Attempting step four before step two is why arrivals take months instead of weeks.
relocation.services.4.conditions.items.0: Address first, then registration, then BSN. Nothing meaningful can be arranged before the BSN exists.
relocation.services.4.conditions.items.1: DigiD, the national login, follows the BSN and is required for the tax office, healthcare and most government services.
relocation.services.4.conditions.items.2: Most Dutch banks require a BSN and proof of address, though some accounts can be opened earlier with a passport alone.
relocation.services.4.conditions.items.3: Health insurance must be taken within four months of registration and is backdated to arrival.
relocation.services.4.conditions.items.4: Energy, water and internet contracts are in your name from the day the lease starts, and switching later carries notice periods.
relocation.services.4.conditions.items.5: Exchanging a foreign driving licence is only possible for some countries, and only within a set period after registration.
relocation.services.4.details.title: The things nobody tells you
relocation.services.4.details.items.0.a: It depends less on the bank than on what you need from it. Mortgage ambitions, business banking, an employer that pays from abroad and family in another currency all point to different answers. We open the account with you and make sure iDEAL, the payment method half the country runs on, works from day one.
relocation.services.4.details.items.1.q: Can I use my foreign driving licence?
relocation.services.4.details.items.1.a: EU and EEA licences remain valid. Licences from a number of other countries, including some US states, can be exchanged without a new test, but only within a limited window after registration and in some cases only if you hold the 30 percent ruling. Miss the window and you sit the full Dutch test. We check your situation early because this deadline is unforgiving.
relocation.services.4.details.items.2.q: How do I get a doctor, dentist and pharmacy?
relocation.services.4.details.items.2.a: You register with a GP practice near your address, and the practice assigns your pharmacy. Both fill up, so both are done in your first fortnight. Dentists take private patients directly and are easier, though good ones in the centre still have lists.
relocation.services.4.details.items.3.q: What about the tax office in year one?
relocation.services.4.details.items.3.a: Your first Dutch tax year is almost always worth filing even when you think nothing is owed, because arrival year filings frequently produce a refund. We are relocation consultants rather than tax advisers, so we introduce you to an adviser who handles expat returns rather than guessing on your behalf.
relocation.services.4.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
relocation.services.4.faq.items.0.q: Can I open a Dutch bank account before I have a BSN?
relocation.services.4.faq.items.0.a: Some banks allow it and let you supply the BSN afterwards; policies change often. We know the current state of play and steer you to the fastest route so your salary has somewhere to land.
relocation.services.4.faq.items.1.q: What is DigiD and do I really need it?
relocation.services.4.faq.items.1.a: DigiD is your digital identity for the Dutch government: taxes, healthcare, allowances and municipal services all use it. You will need it constantly, and we set it up with you early.

relocation.services.6.details.items.1.q: My partner is giving up a career to come. What is realistic?
relocation.services.6.details.items.1.a: The Dutch labour market is genuinely open to accompanying partners, particularly in English-speaking sectors around Rotterdam and The Hague, and no work permit is needed. What helps most is a Dutch-format CV, an understanding of how local recruitment actually works, and starting before the move rather than after. We make the introductions we can.
relocation.services.6.details.items.2.a: Better than parents expect, and on a slower timeline than parents hope. The Dutch system is unusually kind to newcomer children and the nieuwkomersklas works. The harder part is usually months three to six, once the novelty has gone, and it helps enormously to have planned sport, music or a club before you need it.
relocation.services.6.details.items.3.q: Can everything really run in parallel?
relocation.services.6.details.items.3.a: Yes, and it has to. Permits, school applications, housing, registration and insurance each have their own waiting time, so we run them concurrently against one family timeline rather than one after another. That is the difference between a move that takes ten weeks and one that takes six months.
relocation.services.6.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
relocation.services.6.faq.items.0.q: How far in advance should a family start planning?
relocation.services.6.faq.items.0.a: Three to six months before the move is comfortable, mainly because school places and family-sized rentals are the scarcest pieces. Less time than that is workable too; it simply means we prioritize harder from day one.
relocation.services.6.faq.items.1.q: Can you support the visa side of a family move as well?

relocation.services.6.faq.items.2.q: What about our children who are not school-age yet?
relocation.services.6.faq.items.2.a: Daycare in the Netherlands often has longer waiting lists than schools do, so we treat childcare with the same urgency: shortlists, applications and an explanation of the childcare allowance you may be entitled to.

business.services.1.explainer.text.1: That choice drives everything downstream, including how you are taxed, whether you can bring in shareholders, how banks and clients assess you, and in several cases which residence permit you qualify for.
